Improve warnings for undefined variables in templates introduced in #48140

Example: rendering template `"{{ no_such_variable }}"` will result in this error message:
```
"Template variable warning when rendering '{{ no_such_variable }}': 'no_such_variable' is undefined"
```

issue_context.title: Template variable warnings not descriptive enough to debug (2021.4.0b2)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

My logs shows several `template variable warning`s - but there is no way to identify which template is generating these. Could we possibly make these error messages more descriptive?

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.4.0b2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.3.4

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

template

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/template/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-04-02 10:22:33 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute 02/04/2021
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute humidity_alarm
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute battery_low
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute duration
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute temperature_min
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute temperature_max
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute humidity_min
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute humidity_max
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute linkquality
2021-04-02 10:23:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute power_type
```
comments:
Some attributes should be searchable in the configuration, but I have some of these:
```
2021-04-02 10:32:32 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable warning: list object has no element 1
```

Yeah, but the error is complaining about missing attributes, so that's a bit harder to debug :wink:

But I guess your error is also making the point: how to debug that one.

```
Logger: homeassistant.helpers.template
Source: /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/jinja2/runtime.py:873
First occurred: 10:40:05 (8 occurrences)
Last logged: 10:40:07

Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute interlock
Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute action_angle
Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute action_from_side
Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute action_side
Template variable warning: dict object has no attribute action_to_side
```

The warnings are because of #48140.
The warning messages are improved by #48713, the bad template will now be printed as well.

just to add this version of the **_error_** (note: not warning):
```
[homeassistant.helpers.template] Template variable error: 'dict object' has no attribute 'data'
```

believe this is tagged for the 2021.4.0 release, wouldn't this warrant an extra beta update though? such a fundamental change in the logger.

review_comments: Should we set it to `None` after the render?
I was thinking about that. Is there any scenario in which we could print a stale ContextVar?
It's mainly for garbage collection purposes.

It took me a bit to realize, this is wrapping Jinja2 objects. Why don't we store our own template objects in it so we can access the template string too? 

In the future we can then add "names" to templates, ie `sensor.kitchen_temp - attribute name`
